text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Paper and packaging concern KNP BT seeks partner for its paper making unit KNP Leykam. (p1)
- Dutch companies are optimistic and expect a good autumn, according to Central Statistics Bureau's survey. (p1)
- Light engineering sector revamps early retirement scheme. (p1)
- Takeover of bankrupt planemaker Fokker by Samsung is 80 percent certain, says Amsterdam's mayor Schelto Patijn. (p1)
- Transport concern Nedlloyd criticises slowness of container trains. (p3)
- Amsterdam court rules that bank insurer ING does not have to sell plastic disposables concern De Ster to its former owner. (p3)
- ABN Amro Hoare Govett re-issues some 2.4 million shares of automation company CMG. (p4)
- Randstad area wants Dfl 56 bn in the next 10 to 15 years to fight traffic jams. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Council of State wants more clarity from finance ministry on bill against insider trading. (p2)
- Cargo unit of Royal Dutch Airlines KLM to fly to Vienna and Stockholm from October 1. (p2)
- Parliament is against ban on selling tobacco to the underaged. (p3)
- Foreign affairs minister Hans van Mierlo counts of great importance that UN authority will be restored. (p6)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Building and development firm Van Wijnen pulls out of operations in Germany. (p25)
- New pension scheme to be introduced for workers in the metal industry. (p27)
TROUW
- NedCar conducts talks with its works council about extending night shifts. (p7)
- U.S. high-tech concern Cisco to build its European headquarters in Amsterdam. (p18)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Philips Electronics seeks expansion in Asia; company plans to invest Dfl 2.5 bn in next five years. (p11)
- Builder Heijmans wants to take over Exters Beheer of Uden. (p13)
